answers.answer: [HONEST CONCESSION — partial, rule not operational]. My spec states the boundary as a slogan plus two lists: CORE (needle bed, needles, cam systems, electronic needle-selection, controller firmware, knit-CAD) = the 'core kinematic chain' = highest-confidence NEVER; PERIPHERY (jigs, fixtures, alignment gauges, non-critical spares, cam-timing LEARNING, scanning worn obsolete brackets) = OK (glossary 'periphery-only reverse-engineering rule' + 'core kinematic chain'; conflicts_and_dominance[6]; boundaries[2]; KB3 PERIPHERY_REVERSE_ENG line 176/263). There is NO stated operational test to classify a borderline part, so I cannot mechanically adjudicate the three examples — I can only reason toward a test I do not currently own. The operational test I SHOULD state (proposed, not pre-existing): a part is CORE (NEVER reverse-engineer/clone) if ANY of — (1) it sets or holds knit geometry/registration to needle-pitch tolerance (bed, needle, cam-to-needle timing, selection), (2) it touches the yarn path in a way that changes stitch formation, or (3) it embeds vendor firmware/knit-CAD IP; otherwise it is periphery. Applying it: (a) needle-bed ALIGNMENT GAUGE — a measuring jig you USE to check pitch is periphery (allowed: fabricate/scan a gauge to LEARN/verify); but a part you MAKE that itself SETS bed alignment is core -> the discriminator is measure-vs-set. (b) CAM FOLLOWER — rides the cam and drives needle motion to pitch tolerance = criterion (1) knit-geometry-critical -> CORE, do not fabricate/clone; buy OEM. (c) YARN-PATH-TOUCHING CARRIER BRACKET — a purely structural mounting bracket is periphery, but the moment the part touches or positions the yarn path affecting stitch formation it hits criterion (2) -> CORE. The discipline guard is that 'it's just a cheap spare' is NOT a criterion; cost/size never reclassify a part — only measure-vs-set, yarn-path-effect, and IP-embodiment do — which stops the by-increments erosion into core-chain cloning.
